A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PMS-FTP study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, checklist and Appendices A-C are readable and support a complete comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, memory measurements, ablations, scalability experiments and statistical analyses in Section 5 and Appendices A-B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparison, reasoning evaluations, incremental-domain experiment and bootstrap analysis.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the partition objective, discrepancy and synergy measures, stage-wise adapter updates and norm projection remain unchanged. Pruning is suggested only as future work, not introduced into the method.

E1.justification: Both retain the four main tasks, SQuAD/HotpotQA/CNN-DM/XSum slice, Wiki-10/Multi-News mixture, five reasoning benchmarks, Legal-QA extension and synthetic domain-scaling scenarios. Newly cited application papers do not expand evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments. Table 1 retains its full-tuning, domain-adaptation, PEFT and data-selection baselines; Tables 17-18 retain iMTL, FAMO and ExcessMTL alongside FULL, LoRA and Tag-LLM.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A preserve the backbones, dataset splits, metrics, preprocessing, training configurations and full-tuning versus PEFT controls. The supplementary experiments also retain their evaluation designs.

E4.justification: The stage-count, partition, norm and synergy ablations are retained. Appendix analyses of stage ordering, gradient conflicts, noisy affinities, scalability, objective validity, forgetting and centroid robustness also match.

E5.justification: Both retain Figure 2's error bars, the checklist statement about standard deviations across independent runs, Table 16's correlation significance and Table 20's bootstrap confidence intervals. No run-count or seed information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched result tables and plots retain their values and findings. For example, Table 1's LLaMA2-13B PMS-FTP scores remain 43.4/67.2/90.2/88.0, and Tables 17-18 retain reasoning averages of 62.4 and 67.4.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, Lemma 3.1, Theorems 3.1-3.2, Corollary 3.1 and Appendix C proofs are unchanged. Differences in mathematical typesetting and page placement do not alter their content.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about synergy-based partitioning, generalization bounds and accuracy/memory benefits. The added pruning suggestion is not presented as an achieved contribution.

C2.justification: Result interpretations, mechanism explanations and limitations remain unchanged. Section 2.1 makes explicit the simultaneous-versus-sequential distinction already conveyed by v1's introduction and future-work discussion; the pruning suggestion does not revise current applicability or explain existing results.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 retains the hardware, software versions, hyperparameters, preprocessing and implementation instructions. Both checklists state that study code and data are not publicly available because of institutional and proprietary restrictions.

R1.justification: The cited literature expands substantially, with 28 additions and removal of DOA and C3-OWD. Additions span infrastructure, vision/robotics, continual learning and pruning, including explicit positioning in Section 2.1 and future-work links in Section 6. Authorship and year-suffix changes to retained works are separate metadata edits.

P1.justification: Short passages add resource-constraint motivation, a continual-learning comparison and pruning as future work. Author-list punctuation and bibliographic text are edited, but most prose and the section and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All 21 tables and three figures remain. Algorithm 1, Table 1, Table 3 and Figure 2 move, with some table widths and surrounding text wrapping adjusted. The three plot images themselves are identical.

improvement.justification: The scientific evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged. The clearer continual-learning comparison offers a small benefit, but v3 adds unexplained citation connections: Section 1 cites Tao et al. (2023), identified in the bibliography as remote-sensing pan-sharpening, for LLM domain adapters, and Wang and Zhang (2024), about cubic polynomials, for suboptimal multi-domain fine-tuning. These additions weaken the precision of the literature support, producing a limited overall decline.
